faqs.question: What does the Fungal stain test - Skin measure?
faqs.answer: This test detects the presence of fungal elements in skin samples using special stains, KOH & Calcofluor White.

faqs.question: Why is the Fungal stain test - Skin done?
faqs.answer: • To diagnose fungal infections on the skin, hair, or nails • To monitor the effectiveness of treatment for fungal infections • To identify other fungal-related conditions • To assess the risk of developing infections such as candidiasis

faqs.question: When is the Fungal stain test - Skin recommended and who should take the test?
faqs.answer: • Your doctor may recommend this test if you have symptoms suggesting a fungal infection, such as itching, redness, scaling, or discoloured patches on your skin or nails. • This test is suitable for patients with suspected fungal infections and those with known risk factors for fungal-related conditions.

faqs.question: What if the results of the Fungal stain test - Skin are abnormal?
faqs.answer: If the test results show the presence of fungal elements, it suggests a fungal infection.

faqs.question: What to expect during the Fungal stain test - Skin?
faqs.answer: During the test, a small skin sample will be collected in a sterile container. The sample will be sent to the laboratory for processing and staining with KOH & Calcofluor White.

faqs.question: What preparations are required before the Fungal stain test - Skin?
faqs.answer: • Inform your doctor about any medications you are taking. Also, tell them if you have any specific requirements. • Follow any specific instructions provided, such as avoiding antifungal creams or lotions before the test.

faqs.question: What other tests may be ordered with the Fungal stain test - Skin?
faqs.answer: • Fungal culture: This test helps grow fungi from a sample to identify the specific type causing the infection. • Antifungal susceptibility testing: It determines which antifungal medications will be effective against the identified fungus. • PCR testing: Polymerase chain reaction (PCR) detects and identifies fungal DNA, aiding in accurate diagnosis.

faqs.question: What is the Fungal stain by KOH & Calcofluor White stain - Skin also known as?
What is a fungal infection?
faqs.answer: A fungal infection is caused by different types of fungi and can affect various parts of the body, including the skin, hair, and nails. It manifests as itching, redness, scaling, or discoloured patches.
